sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A stemless mountain aloe endemic to Lesotho’s Maluti Mountains. Its many toothed leaves form a spiral rosette that can reach about 50–80 cm across in old plants. It grows on moist, often mist-shrouded basalt slopes, generally above 2,000 m. Branched flower stalks can reach 50–60 cm and bear pink-orange flowers.

sections.title: Uses and conservation
sections.text: No food use is established in the sources consulted. This high-altitude species is distinct from desert-growing aloes.
